speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing swelling in your right knee and have a family history of similar issues. To begin our evaluation, can you describe exactly when the swelling started and what specific activities, if any, triggered the onset of pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease. The patient is an 18-month-old boy with right knee swelling, no trauma, and a family history of similar issues, which strongly suggests a self-limiting avascular necrosis of the femoral head rather than septic arthritis or trauma.
